haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes into the shadow store, which holds its non-authoritative invoices.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes its invoices into the shadow store and does not charge.
haiku-low.q3: Gates met: 7 consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and 5000+ invoices compared. Then handoff steps run. A person sends the move command.
haiku-low.q4: Charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window, in both or new_only. In new_only, automatic rollback also works only before day 35.
haiku-low.q5: Always old_only. The new engine stays blocked until a person moves to shadow, which deletes the rollback record. Then a fresh handoff to both.
haiku-low.q6: After 35 days in new_only. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so skipped events expire and replay cannot catch up.
haiku-low.q7: How often workers re-read the flag is NOT STATED. Mode moves wait for acknowledgements. What happens to an invoice mid-processing is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: Nightly comparison results, saved in a comparison table outside the ledger. The controller rejects forward moves whose gates are unmet. Direct flag edits may bypass this; NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q9: The controller measures charge failure rate over a rolling 10-minute window. Above 2%, it starts an automatic rollback.
haiku-low.q10: They are delayed, not skipped. Rollback step 5 charges already-due ones via the old engine. Later ones are charged after the flag says old_only.
haiku-low.q11: The old engine checks the ledger and skips periods already charged. The charge key lets the provider refuse a repeat charge.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays in RollingBack, new charging paused, flag unchanged. The step retries in place, paging on-call if retries keep failing.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine computes invoices from the same usage events into the shadow store. It never charges or writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine keeps computing invoices into the shadow store (for comparison and rollback) and does not charge.
sonnet.q3: Gates must be met: 7 consecutive days under 0.1% mismatch and 5000+ invoices compared (the controller checks this once at the start of the move). Then the handoff runs: write the handoff record, wait for live old-engine instances to acknowledge, settle in-flight old charges, write the both entry time, set the flag. A person makes the move by sending a command to the controller. The exact mechanism (command, UI or config edit) is an open question.
sonnet.q4: A charge failure rate above 2% in any 10-minute window triggers an automatic rollback. This applies in both and new_only (new_only only before day 35). In shadow, rollback is manual only.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. The gates are reset and the 7-day count restarts at zero. The rollback record stays and the new engine stays blocked until a person moves old_only to shadow, which deletes the record. The rollout must then pass through shadow and the gates again.
sonnet.q6: It stops at day 35 after entering new_only (new_only_locked). Usage events are kept only 35 days, so the skipped events needed for replay would expire. A rollback that started before day 35 may finish.
sonnet.q7: Workers and both engines read the single billing_mode flag in the config service. How often they re-read it is NOT STATED (an open question). For an invoice in flight at that moment: charges that passed the check just before the record appeared may still be in flight. The controller waits for each to reach a known outcome, looks up unknowns at the provider by charge key without blind resubmit, and ensures every confirmed charge has a ledger row before moving on.
sonnet.q8: The evidence is the nightly comparison results, saved as one row per customer per night. They are assumed to be in a comparison results table outside the ledger. The controller computes the gate counters from them, starting at the gates-reset-at timestamp. The controller rejects forward-move commands whose gates are not met. A person who edits the flag directly in the config service could bypass this, and whether that is prevented is not known.
sonnet.q9: The controller measures the charge failure rate. This is assumed to be failed charges divided by attempted charges over a rolling 10-minute window. Where it gets the counts is not known. When the rate is above 2% in both or new_only, it starts an automatic rollback: it writes the rollback record and runs the rollback steps.
sonnet.q10: The new engine is blocked from charging for the whole rollback, so charges that fall due are late, not lost. They are made in rollback step 5, when the old engine's charge-due run charges every closed period that has a finished invoice and no ledger charge. Anything that falls due after step 5 and before the flag changes is charged by the old engine's normal run once the flag says old_only.
sonnet.q11: Before charging a period, the old engine checks the ledger. If the new engine already charged that period, it does not charge it. The charge key (customer plus billing period) is also sent to the provider as an idempotency key, so a second charge for the same key is refused. In-flight charges are settled first, and every provider-confirmed charge must have a ledger row.
sonnet.q12: The controller stays in RollingBack and the rollback record remains. New charging stays paused and the flag is not set until the ledger is consistent. The failed step is retried in place. The controller pages on-call if retries keep failing. If the controller crashes, it resumes from the stored step, and each step is safe to repeat. Forward moves are rejected until the record says done. The exact retry limits and back-off are not specified.
